citation.title: A Parametric Level Set Method for Topology Optimization based on Deep Neural Network (DNN)
citation.version_coded: arXiv full text; version not stated in retrieved PDF

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For MBB and short-cantilever compliance examples, DNN level-set designs have compliance close to or slightly better than SIMP benchmark designs.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No speed or computational-cost comparison is reported.
claim.alternatives: Section 4 reports stable solutions after 120–150 iterations for some architectures, but no classical runtime comparison.

baseline.problem_size: MBB beam: 200 × 100 elements; short cantilever: 100 × 100 elements (Sections 4.1–4.2)
baseline.quality_gap: MBB: one-hidden-layer and two-hidden-layer networks described as close to SIMP compliance 33.48; two/three hidden-layer short-cantilever designs reported around 3.5% below the benchmark (Sections 4.1–4.2).

R1.evidence: Sections 4.1–4.2 compare compliance/design quality; no speed comparison is made.

R2.evidence: Section 4 compares compliance only and reports no comparative runtime.

R3.evidence: Section 3 updates network parameters within each optimization; no offline training cost is claimed.

R4.evidence: Sections 4.1–4.2 report compliance for returned designs and formulate volume constraints, but do not report infeasibility or failure rates.

reporting.n_test_cases: Three benchmark problem setups (MBB beam, short cantilever, and additional architecture variants; Sections 4.1–4.2)
